title: BNP Paribas Volunteers Head to Peru to Support The community of Children Sagrada Familia
description: In May 2019, five BNP Paribas employees had the unique opportunity to bring their professional skills to support an orphanage in Peru.  The inaugural BNP Paribas Fellowship Program was a unique initiative for employees to share their skills and expertise with underserved communities through a meaningful gift of their time. These five BNP Paribas employees volunteered to support La Comunidad de Ninos Sagrada Familia, one of the largest youth centers in Peru, hosting a school, an orphanage and a daycare clinic. They helped improve the daily lives of the 1,500 children.  Some meaningful initiatives included: • On the accounting front, the team identified all expenses and revenues and create a tool to capture all transactions. Staff were trained on this tool and weekly follow-ups were scheduled to continue the set-up.  • In terms of infrastructure, the priority was to find a solution to have running water. The team brought in a contractor and a plumbing engineer to assess solutions for the water situation. Important improvements were also made in the kitchen area, where two industrial refrigerators were repaired that are now up and running like new, and a new roof over the main pantry was installed.  • On the marketing side, their website was completely redesigned. A Facebook page and a video to present the structure were also created. Additionally, BNP Paribas employees who could not participate in-person held fundraising events, including an employee concert, yoga classes and a trivia night. Over USD 60,000 was raised and provided to the youth center!

The fellowship program constituted of five people that went to Lima, Peru to help an orphanage called. Sagrada Familia for two weeks. Miguel created La Sagrada Familia over 30 years ago because he. Wanted to provide a safe haven for children who didn't have a place to go. Lily joined the cause. To help manage the orphanage and Lily and Miguel are really the mom and dad of La Comunidad. La Sagrada Familia is like a big family where all the children become your brothers and sisters. The two main events that take place on a daily basis in the community are mealtime and school. Time. The length of the meal time preparation alone is about five hours a day. Unfortunately,. La Sagrada Familia is facing difficulties surrounding the lack of water, electricity,. And the issues with security. So I applied to this program to see what type of impact I could have. Outside of the financial sector. Our group of five came in to make an external analysis on the most. Needed improvements and propose ways to implement those. Living on site and spending time with the. Children allowed us to assess firsthand what needed investment and renovation immediately. So some days at the orphanage are spent without any electricity because of the obsolescence of. The installations and because of that lack of electricity the pumps are not running and the. Water is not available either. It was painful to see little boys and girls carrying buckets of. Water for a long distance just to get basic sanitation. There are definitely issues of. Physical security. The orphanage is located in a community that's extremely poor, so everything has. Value including water, electricity. So one thing that we did for them is we built an accounting. System and we trained them to use it. I brought some contacts to help with the renovation of the. Infrastructure and through a colleague at BNPP Peru, he was able to onboard some lawyers to assist. In clarifying the legal and tax situation. We built a website to help the orphanage present themselves outside of Lima,. As well to fundraise on different projects. La Comunidad deserves to be well known and well supported. We'd like to thank them for opening their hearts to us and making us part of the family. I'm grateful that BNP Paribas allowed us the opportunity to leave work behind and really. Work on the ground to help the children and the community. We left as a group of five people who didn't know each other and over the course of two weeks we. Connected and we created a working community that continues today. I'm very proud and happy with that.
